sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Yonkers, New York?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell the house yourself, or take a cash offer on it as it stands. Yonkers sellers should plan for one cost that is specific to the city: a local transfer tax of 1.5 percent of the sale price, paid by the seller on top of the state tax.

Yonkers sits in Westchester County directly north of the Bronx, and the Census Bureau estimates 212,603 residents as of July 1, 2025. That makes it the largest city in the county. Most delays in a Yonkers sale come from three places: the city's property files, the tax installments, and the transfer tax return that has to be stamped before the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Yonkers housing?
sections.html:
Fewer than half of Yonkers households own the home they live in, which means rental buildings and small multifamily houses are a large part of what changes hands.

sections.h2: What is the layout of Yonkers, and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Yonkers covers about 18 square miles of land. The Hudson River is its western edge, the Bronx River separates it from Mount Vernon, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale on the east, and the Bronx lies to the south. The ground climbs from near sea level at the river to 416 feet at Sacred Heart Church, and the city is known as the City of Seven Hills. The Saw Mill River divides the city into four quarters and joins the Hudson at Getty Square, the downtown and civic center.

The land was part of a Dutch grant made in 1645 to Adriaen van der Donck, and the name comes from his local title, Jonkheer. Yonkers became a village in 1854 and a city in 1872. The Otis Elevator Company opened what is described as the first elevator factory here after 1853, and the Alexander Smith carpet mills grew to more than 4,000 workers. When the five boroughs consolidated in 1898, Yonkers stayed out.

  • Northeast: Crestwood, Colonial Heights, Cedar Knolls and Lawrence Park West, near several Metro-North stations.
  • Northwest: Nepera Park, Runyon Heights, Homefield, Glenwood and Greystone, with Victorian houses and Palisades views.
  • Southeast: Dunwoodie and the McLean Avenue area, where building styles resemble those in the Bronx and Queens.
  • Southwest: Getty Square, Park Hill, Nodine Hill, Lowerre and Hudson Park, a mix of apartments, row houses and detached homes.

sections.h2: How do trains, jobs and flooding history affect a Yonkers sale?
sections.html:
Transit is a strong draw. Hudson Line stations at Ludlow, Yonkers, Glenwood and Greystone carry commuters to Manhattan, and the Yonkers station is also served by Amtrak's Empire Service trains. Harlem Line stations sit along the eastern border. Yonkers has the eleventh-highest rate of public transit ridership among US cities, and 27 percent of households have no car. Roads include I-87 and the Saw Mill, Bronx River, Sprain Brook and Cross County parkways.

Local employers listed in the city's 2024 annual financial report include St. John's Riverside Hospital (1,939 jobs), St. Joseph's Medical Center (1,027), Liberty Lines, Kawasaki Rail, Consumer Reports and Lionsgate. On September 29, 2023, flash flooding led the city to declare a state of emergency, and crews pumped water out of houses afterward. If your basement took water, expect questions from the buyer's inspector and insurer, and keep repair records.

sections.h2: What does the Yonkers Department of Housing and Buildings handle?
sections.html:
The department issues building permits and certificates of occupancy, runs inspections and investigates complaints. Permit applications are filed online through the City Squared portal.

  • Before a permit is issued to renovate an existing one- to three-family dwelling, the city requires a Home Improvement Contractor's License, available from the Consumer Protection Bureau.
  • Property records are viewed by appointment. Have the block and lot ready. The department is digitizing its paper files and emails a link to the documents rather than asking you to visit.
  • The link can arrive after the appointment date, so request files before you list.

Older Yonkers houses often have additions and finished basements, and the file is where a buyer's attorney will look for the matching permits.

sections.h2: How does the Yonkers property tax bill work?
sections.html:
A Yonkers homeowner receives two bills a year. The county bill arrives in March and is paid once, with a due date in April. For 2026 it was April 14. The City and School bill arrives in July and is split into three equal installments.

  • First installment for 2026/27: Friday, July 24, 2026 (passed).
  • Second installment: Tuesday, October 6, 2026 (passed).
  • Third installment: Wednesday, January 6, 2027.

The city sets the first date 30 days after its budget is adopted, and the later two dates are always October 6 and January 6, moved if they fall on a weekend. There is no grace period. Late installments accrue 15 percent annual interest, calculated daily from the confirmation date, and the city says interest cannot be waived. Timeliness is judged by the postmark on the envelope.

Title and mortgage companies can research a parcel online for free, or request a tax search from the Tax Office for $5 per property per year. The city asks for a two to three week lead time, so order early. Payments go to City Hall, Room 108, 40 South Broadway.

sections.h2: When can you contest a Yonkers assessment?
sections.html:
The Assessment Department's calendar is fixed, and the filing window is only two weeks long.

  • October 15: taxable status date, and the deadline to file or renew senior, disability and veterans exemptions.
  • November 1: tentative roll published.
  • November 1 to November 15: grievance period for the Board of Assessment Review.
  • December 15: deadline to add information or request a personal hearing.
  • Late January to the third Friday in February: hearings.
  • April 10: final roll. From April 10 to May 10, owners who already protested may file for Small Claims Assessment Review with the county.

Because the window closes on November 15 each year, a missed date means waiting a full year.

sections.h2: What do sellers owe at closing in Yonkers?
sections.html:
The city's transfer tax is 1.5 percent of the selling price and falls on the seller. No tax is due on a sale of $25,000 or less, and co-op unit sales are not charged. The tax must be paid within seven days after the deed is delivered and before it is recorded. Both seller and buyer file a return, even when no tax is due.

The process runs in order: file the return, pay, receive a stamped receipt from the city, then take the receipt to the Westchester County Clerk to record the deed. The city recommends emailing the return and receipt to its transfer tax office, since that is the quickest way to get the stamp. Mailed copies go to City Hall, Room 108.

On the median owner-occupied value of $501,600, the city tax comes to $7,524. New York's base tax adds $2 per $500 of price, rounded up, and the buyer pays an extra 1 percent mansion tax at $1 million and above. File Form TP-584 with the county clerk within 15 days of delivering the deed.

faqs.q: How much is the Yonkers transfer tax on a $500,000 house?
faqs.a: It is $7,500, which is 1.5 percent of the price. The seller pays it to the city, and it is due within seven days after the deed is delivered and before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: When is the next Yonkers City tax installment due?
faqs.a: The third installment of the 2026/27 City and School bill is due Wednesday, January 6, 2027. The July 24 and October 6, 2026 installments have already passed.

faqs.q: Does Yonkers charge interest if I pay a day late?
faqs.a: Yes. The city has no grace period and charges 15 percent annual interest from the confirmation date, calculated daily. It says interest cannot be waived for any reason.

faqs.q: How do I get the building file for my Yonkers house?
faqs.a: Make an appointment with the Department of Housing and Buildings using the block and lot number. The department then emails a link to the available paper and digital documents.

faqs.q: Where is a Yonkers deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Westchester County Clerk. Yonkers issues its own transfer tax receipt first, and that receipt must be filed with the clerk to have the deed recorded.
